user_questions.question: How should zones relate to storefronts? (a) each zone belongs to one storefront (Master-Detail child of Storefront__c); (b) zones are shared records linked to storefronts through a Storefront-to-Zone junction (many-to-many); (c) reuse the existing empty Region__c object (0 records, only Onboarding_Specialist__c). Evidence: no zone object exists; Region__c exists but is an onboarding concept.
user_questions.simulated_answer: (b) Shared zones with a storefront-zone junction.

user_questions.question: How should a zone's zip codes be stored? (a) one child record per zip code (filterable, enforceable uniqueness); (b) a zip code list field on the zone record. Evidence: no zip field or object exists; Storefront__c.Address__c is only the storefront's own address.

How should the fee be charged? No order or cart object exists and Transaction__c has no Storefront__c lookup. (a) store the fee on the zone only; applying it to orders is out of scope here (recommended); (b) also build a fee lookup (for example an invocable action returning the fee for storefront + zip); (c) add the fee to Transaction__c.
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: validate_spec.py rejects two changes with the same API name even when their types differ; a CustomTab for a custom object necessarily shares the object's API name (Delivery_Zone__c), so the tab had to be dropped from the inventory and moved to Section 8. The format spec says 'Section 9 lists the same (Action, API name) pairs, each once' without saying how to handle tab/object or other same-name components of different types.

Module rule says 'the known force-app/... path or Not specified. Do not invent paths.' With force-app empty, it is unclear whether standard source-format paths (force-app/main/default/objects/...) for new components count as known or invented; I used the standard paths and noted the Storefront layout must be retrieved first.
The I template has no slot for scope-check decisions to be sent as decisions vs facts; AskCoworker tagged user decisions as [Verified: user decision], blurring the source labels.

AskCoworker repeatedly reported 'prior session' facts (data streams, ObjectPermissions) despite the ignore-earlier-conversations header; the skill says verify them, but gives no guidance for facts like DataStreamDefinition that the allowed commands cannot query.

Step 5 lists 'cannot deliver a responsibility end to end' as an ask trigger, but when the simulated user answers 'no preference', the skill does not say whether deferring the responsibility as a recommended default is acceptable or counts as 'silently deferring to another spec'.

The R answer asserted a platform behavior (cascade-deleted details are not restored on master undelete) that contradicts documented behavior; Rule 3 covers rejecting proposals that depend on it, but not where to record a factual correction that no query can test — I put it in Section 8.
